name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q01 - Matching vitamins with their deficiency diseases

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Vitamin) List-II (Deficiency Disease)
(A) Vitamin A(I) Beri beri
(B) Vitamin B1(II) Convulsions
(C) Vitamin C(III) Xerophthalmia
(D) Vitamin B6(IV) Scurvy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Vitamin A deficiency leads to xerophthalmia (hardening of cornea of eye) and night blindness.

Step 2
Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency results in beri beri, characterized by loss of appetite and retarded growth.

Step 3
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency causes scurvy, which is manifested by bleeding gums.

Step 4
Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) deficiency leads to convulsions.

Final Answer
Vitamin A pairs with Xerophthalmia; Vitamin B1 pairs with Beri beri; Vitamin C pairs with Scurvy; and Vitamin B6 pairs with Convulsions.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q02 - Classification and examples of dietary carbohydrates

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Carbohydrate) List-II (Classification / Type)
(A) Glucose(I) Main storage polysaccharide of plants
(B) Sucrose(II) Ketohexose monosaccharide
(C) Fructose(III) Aldohexose monosaccharide
(D) Starch(IV) Disaccharide yielding glucose and fructose

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Glucose is an aldohexose monomer having the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) with an aldehyde functional group and five hydroxyl groups.

Step 2
Sucrose is a common disaccharide that on hydrolysis gives an equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose.

Step 3
Fructose is a natural ketohexose monosaccharide containing a ketonic functional group at carbon-2.

Step 4
Starch is the primary storage polysaccharide of plants, consisting of amylose and amylopectin polymers of \(\alpha\)-glucose.

Final Answer
Glucose pairs with Aldohexose monosaccharide; Sucrose pairs with Disaccharide yielding glucose and fructose; Fructose pairs with Ketohexose monosaccharide; and Starch pairs with Main storage polysaccharide of plants.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q03 - Reactions of glucose and structural deductions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reaction of Glucose) List-II (Structural Inference / Product)
(A) Prolonged heating with \(\mathrm{HI}\)(I) Formation of gluconic acid indicating an aldehydic group
(B) Reaction with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) water(II) Formation of saccharic acid indicating a primary alcoholic group
(C) Oxidation with concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)(III) Formation of pentaacetate indicating five \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups
(D) Reaction with acetic anhydride(IV) Formation of \(n\)-hexane indicating a continuous six-carbon chain

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Heating glucose with hydroiodic acid (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) for a prolonged period yields \(n\)-hexane, which confirms that all six carbon atoms are joined in an unbranched straight chain.

Step 2
Reaction of glucose with a mild oxidising agent such as bromine water oxidises the terminal carbonyl group to a carboxyl group, forming gluconic acid, which confirms that the carbonyl group is an aldehyde.

Step 3
Oxidation of glucose with nitric acid oxidises both the terminal aldehyde and the primary alcohol group to dicarboxylic acid (saccharic acid), proving the presence of a primary alcoholic group.

Step 4
Acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride gives a stable pentaacetate derivative, confirming that glucose contains five hydroxyl groups attached to distinct carbon atoms.

Final Answer
Prolonged heating with \(\mathrm{HI}\) pairs with Formation of \(n\)-hexane indicating a continuous six-carbon chain; Reaction with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) water pairs with Formation of gluconic acid indicating an aldehydic group; Oxidation with concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) pairs with Formation of saccharic acid indicating a primary alcoholic group; and Reaction with acetic anhydride pairs with Formation of pentaacetate indicating five \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q04 - Levels of protein organization and denaturation

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Structural Level / Feature) List-II (Description / Key Characteristic)
(A) Primary structure(I) Spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits
(B) Secondary structure(II) Destruction of \(2^\circ\) and \(3^\circ\) structures while \(1^\circ\) remains intact
(C) Quaternary structure(III) Regular folding into \(\alpha\)-helix or \(\beta\)-pleated sheet by hydrogen bonds
(D) Denaturation of protein(IV) Sequence in which specific amino acids are linked in a polypeptide

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Primary structure refers to the exact linear sequence of amino acids covalently linked by peptide bonds along a polypeptide chain.

Step 2
Secondary structure refers to the localized conformation assumed by the polypeptide backbone, predominantly stabilized by intramolecular or intermolecular hydrogen bonds into \(\alpha\)-helices or \(\beta\)-pleated sheets.

Step 3
Quaternary structure describes the geometric and spatial assembly of two or more separate polypeptide subunits relative to one another in oligomeric proteins.

Step 4
Denaturation is the process wherein physical factors (such as temperature) or chemical factors (such as pH change) disrupt hydrogen bonds and tertiary conformations, causing loss of biological activity while leaving the primary covalent peptide backbone intact.

Final Answer
Primary structure pairs with Sequence in which specific amino acids are linked in a polypeptide; Secondary structure pairs with Regular folding into \(\alpha\)-helix or \(\beta\)-pleated sheet by hydrogen bonds; Quaternary structure pairs with Spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits; and Denaturation of protein pairs with Destruction of \(2^\circ\) and \(3^\circ\) structures while \(1^\circ\) remains intact.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q05 - Solubility characteristics and deficiency of vitamins

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Vitamin) List-II (Deficiency Sign / Characteristic)
(A) Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)(I) Increased blood clotting time
(B) Vitamin B12(II) Cheilosis and burning sensation of skin
(C) Vitamin E(III) Pernicious anaemia; water soluble but stored in the body
(D) Vitamin K(IV) Increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Deficiency of vitamin B2 (riboflavin) causes cheilosis (fissuring at the corners of the mouth and lips), digestive disorders, and a burning sensation of the skin.

Step 2
Vitamin B12 is unique among water-soluble vitamins because it can be stored in the body; its deficiency results in pernicious anaemia (red blood cells deficient in haemoglobin).

Step 3
Deficiency of vitamin E (a fat-soluble antioxidant vitamin) leads to increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness.

Step 4
Vitamin K is essential for blood coagulation; its deficiency results in delayed coagulation and increased blood clotting time.

Final Answer
Vitamin B2 pairs with Cheilosis and burning sensation of skin; Vitamin B12 pairs with Pernicious anaemia; water soluble but stored in the body; Vitamin E pairs with Increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness; and Vitamin K pairs with Increased blood clotting time.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q06 - Chemical nature and biological functions of hormones

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Hormone) List-II (Nature / Physiological Role)
(A) Insulin(I) Iodinated tyrosine derivative regulating basal metabolism
(B) Thyroxine(II) Polypeptide hormone keeping blood glucose within narrow limits
(C) Glucocorticoids(III) Steroid hormone preparing uterus for implantation of fertilised egg
(D) Progesterone(IV) Adrenal cortical steroids controlling carbohydrate metabolism and stress

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Insulin is a polypeptide hormone produced by the pancreas that lowers elevated blood glucose and maintains it within narrow physiological limits.

Step 2
Thyroxine is an iodinated amino acid derivative synthesized from tyrosine in the thyroid gland; abnormally low levels cause hypothyroidism.

Step 3
Glucocorticoids are steroid hormones produced by the adrenal cortex that regulate carbohydrate metabolism, modulate inflammatory responses, and manage stress.

Step 4
Progesterone is a female steroid sex hormone responsible for preparing and maintaining the uterine lining for implantation of the fertilised egg.

Final Answer
Insulin pairs with Polypeptide hormone keeping blood glucose within narrow limits; Thyroxine pairs with Iodinated tyrosine derivative regulating basal metabolism; Glucocorticoids pairs with Adrenal cortical steroids controlling carbohydrate metabolism and stress; and Progesterone pairs with Steroid hormone preparing uterus for implantation of fertilised egg.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q07 - Components and bonds in nucleic acid architecture

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Component / Entity) List-II (Chemical Definition / Structure)
(A) Nucleoside(I) Linkage joining \(5'\) and \(3'\) carbons of adjacent pentose sugars
(B) Nucleotide(II) Unit formed by attachment of a nitrogenous base to \(1'\)-position of sugar
(C) Phosphodiester bond(III) Base pairing between adenine and thymine, or guanine and cytosine
(D) Complementary base pairing(IV) Unit containing base, pentose sugar, and phosphate at \(5'\)-position

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
A nucleoside is a molecular unit formed exclusively by the attachment of a purine or pyrimidine heterocyclic base to the \(1'\)-carbon of a pentose sugar moiety.

Step 2
A nucleotide is formed when a nucleoside is esterified with phosphoric acid at the \(5'\)-position of the pentose sugar.

Step 3
Phosphodiester linkages connect consecutive nucleotide units between the \(5'\)-hydroxyl of one sugar unit and the \(3'\)-hydroxyl of the adjoining sugar unit to construct polynucleotide chains.

Step 4
Complementary base pairing in double-helical DNA relies on specific hydrogen bonding between adenine and thymine, and between guanine and cytosine.

Final Answer
Nucleoside pairs with Unit formed by attachment of a nitrogenous base to \(1'\)-position of sugar; Nucleotide pairs with Unit containing base, pentose sugar, and phosphate at \(5'\)-position; Phosphodiester bond pairs with Linkage joining \(5'\) and \(3'\) carbons of adjacent pentose sugars; and Complementary base pairing pairs with Base pairing between adenine and thymine, or guanine and cytosine.

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Carbohydrate) List-II (Constituent Units and Glycosidic Linkage)
(A) Sucrose(I) Linear \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) \(\alpha\)-glucose chain with branching at \(\mathrm{C1-C6}\)
(B) Lactose(II) \(\beta\)-D-Galactose and \(\beta\)-D-glucose linked via \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) glycosidic bond
(C) Cellulose(III) \(\alpha\)-D-Glucose \(\mathrm{C1}\) linked to \(\beta\)-D-fructose \(\mathrm{C2}\)
(D) Amylopectin(IV) Straight chain of \(\beta\)-D-glucose units joined by \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) glycosidic bond

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide composed of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose and \(\beta\)-D-fructose, held together by a glycosidic linkage between \(\mathrm{C1}\) of glucose and \(\mathrm{C2}\) of fructose.

Step 2
Lactose (milk sugar) is a reducing disaccharide composed of \(\beta\)-D-galactose and \(\beta\)-D-glucose linked through a glycosidic bond between \(\mathrm{C1}\) of galactose and \(\mathrm{C4}\) of glucose.

Step 3
Cellulose is an unbranched structural polysaccharide composed exclusively of \(\beta\)-D-glucose residues joined together by \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) glycosidic linkages.

Step 4
Amylopectin is the water-insoluble fraction of starch; it features a linear chain of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units linked by \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) glycosidic bonds, with branching occurring via \(\mathrm{C1-C6}\) glycosidic linkages.

Final Answer
Sucrose pairs with \(\alpha\)-D-Glucose \(\mathrm{C1}\) linked to \(\beta\)-D-fructose \(\mathrm{C2}\); Lactose pairs with \(\beta\)-D-Galactose and \(\beta\)-D-glucose linked via \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) glycosidic bond; Cellulose pairs with Straight chain of \(\beta\)-D-glucose units joined by \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) glycosidic bond; and Amylopectin pairs with Linear \(\mathrm{C1-C4}\) \(\alpha\)-glucose chain with branching at \(\mathrm{C1-C6}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q09 - Structural characteristics and side chains of amino acids

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Amino Acid) List-II (Side Chain \(-\mathrm{R}\) / Specific Property)
(A) Glycine(I) Side chain \(-\mathrm{CH_2-SH}\); sulfur-containing neutral amino acid
(B) Lysine(II) Side chain \(-\mathrm{H}\); achiral and optically inactive
(C) Glutamic acid(III) Side chain \(-(\mathrm{CH_2})_4-\mathrm{NH_2}\); basic essential amino acid
(D) Cysteine(IV) Side chain \(-\mathrm{CH_2-CH_2-COOH}\); acidic amino acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Glycine possesses a hydrogen atom as its side chain (\(-\mathrm{R} = -\mathrm{H}\)), making its \(\alpha\)-carbon non-asymmetric; hence, it is the only naturally occurring optically inactive \(\alpha\)-amino acid.

Step 2
Lysine contains a butylamino group in its side chain (\(-(\mathrm{CH_2})_4-\mathrm{NH_2}\)), giving it two amino groups versus one carboxyl group, classifying it as a basic essential amino acid.

Step 3
Glutamic acid contains a second carboxylic acid group in its side chain (\(-\mathrm{CH_2-CH_2-COOH}\)), classifying it as a dicarboxylic acidic amino acid.

Step 4
Cysteine contains a thiol group in its side chain (\(-\mathrm{CH_2-SH}\)), making it a sulfur-bearing neutral amino acid involved in disulphide linkage formation.

Final Answer
Glycine pairs with Side chain \(-\mathrm{H}\); achiral and optically inactive; Lysine pairs with Side chain \(-(\mathrm{CH_2})_4-\mathrm{NH_2}\); basic essential amino acid; Glutamic acid pairs with Side chain \(-\mathrm{CH_2-CH_2-COOH}\); acidic amino acid; and Cysteine pairs with Side chain \(-\mathrm{CH_2-SH}\); sulfur-containing neutral amino acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MATCHING_Q10 - Structural forms and functional attributes of biomolecules

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Biomolecular Term / Entity) List-II (Defining Feature / Chemical Property)
(A) Anomers(I) Lowers activation energy of sucrose hydrolysis to \(2.15\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)
(B) Zwitter ion(II) Equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose with net laevorotation
(C) Invert sugar(III) Diastereomers differing only in configuration at \(\mathrm{C1}\) hemiacetal carbon
(D) Sucrase(IV) Dipolar neutral species demonstrating amphoteric chemical behaviour

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1
Anomers are cyclic hemiacetal isomers (such as \(\alpha\)- and \(\beta\)-D-glucose) that differ in configuration specifically at the carbonyl carbon before cyclisation (the anomeric carbon, \(\mathrm{C1}\)).

Step 2
A zwitter ion is an internal dipolar salt formed by proton transfer from the carboxyl group to the amino group, bearing both positive and negative charges, and displaying amphoteric reactivity.

Step 3
Invert sugar refers to the equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-)-fructose produced upon sucrose hydrolysis; because the laevorotation of fructose (\(-92.4^\circ\)) exceeds the dextrorotation of glucose (\(+52.5^\circ\)), the net optical rotation inverts from dextro to laevo.

Step 4
Sucrase is an enzyme biocatalyst that reduces the activation energy for the hydrolysis of sucrose from \(6.22\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) (for acid hydrolysis) down to \(2.15\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Final Answer
Anomers pairs with Diastereomers differing only in configuration at \(\mathrm{C1}\) hemiacetal carbon; Zwitter ion pairs with Dipolar neutral species demonstrating amphoteric chemical behaviour; Invert sugar pairs with Equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose with net laevorotation; and Sucrase pairs with Lowers activation energy of sucrose hydrolysis to \(2.15\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).
